news.title: Fifa’s World Cup TV rights documents indicate hydration breaks to stay in 2030
news.lede: Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters. Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made. Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup include a provision for broadcasters to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication the controversial ­stoppages will be retained. A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.

news.title: Not even Dani Carvajal's absurd trophy cabinet can erase this World Cup regret
news.lede: Former Real Madrid defender Dani Carvajal spoke to Sexta Deportes about not being in the World Cup squad and how that was very sad for him personally in a recent interview.Carvajal is a player who has won almost everything under the sun as a football player. If you talk about the Euros, he was one of the best players in the last edition of the competition. He played out of his mind and won it in a season which was already very trophy-laden for him. He has won the Champions League countless times.

news.title: Uli Hoeneß takes jab at Julian Nagelsmann’s handling of World Cup
news.lede: Uli Hoeneß is already making it pretty clear what he expects from Jürgen Klopp’s Germany tenure, and there might be a little side-eye directed toward the previous regime in the process. Hoeneß believes Klopp will bring discipline, hunger, and a renewed sense of urgency to the national team, while taking a subtle shot at Julian Nagelsmann’s approach to team culture, particularly the infamous family-oriented World Cup camp. ”I don’t think there will be another family outing with player wives and children under Jürgen. I believe he will bring discipline and hunger back.

news.title: U17 World Cup: 10 best wonderkids to watch including Spain gem already breaking Lamine Yamal's records
news.lede: The FIFA U17 World Cup gets underway in Qatar on November 19th, with 48 nations competing for global recognition and the opportunity to showcase football's next generation of superstars. The tournament has historically provided an early glimpse of players who go on to reach the very top, with Phil Foden, Toni Kroos, Cesc Fabregas and Victor Osimhen among those who have previously featured at the competition. Portugal, England, Germany and Nigeria are among the notable absentees this time around, but there is still plenty of emerging talent to get excited about, with representatives from Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Barcelona and Manchester United among the names attracting attention. With matches taking place across the Aspire Zone complex in Doha before the final at Ahmad bin Ali Stadium on December 13th, Football Whispers picks out 10 young talents worth knowing about below.

news.title: Madrid Football Federation Chief on World Cup 2030: ‘Comparison with Morocco Is Insulting’
news.lede: Rabat - Controversial, discriminatory, and hostile remarks by Spaniards targeting Morocco and politicizing sports, particularly the 2030 World Cup final, continue in an apparent attempt to pressure FIFA into awarding Spain the hosting rights for the tournament's final. Following hostile remarks from the PP leader, Spain's football federation, and journalists, it is now the turn of Paco Díez, president of the Royal Madrid Football Federation (RFFM), who went as far as claiming Madrid deserves the title of “the capital of world football.” El Mundo Deportivo quoted Díez, who joined several of his fellow Spaniards in claiming that “comparing ourselves to Morocco would almost be an insult to Spain .” The news outlet said Díez made his remarks during the first roundtable discussion of the “2030 Madrid World Capital?”

news.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
news.lede: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry. The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.
